scope: Proposition 10.5 (The two absolute readings required for the height gap) of the manuscript “Uniform real Lipschitz surfaces on the triangular lattice” (preprints/Uniform-real-Lipschitz-surfaces-on-the-triangular-lattice-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dce5ae39087f446a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 96. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the harmonic- mean compactness and common-sign trace comparison of Proposition 5.8, Theorem 4.1, and The- orem 6.8. Assume also the landing exclusions (10.1) and the sampled-configuration estimates of Proposition 9.10 and Lemma 9.11. Then, along any joint subsequence of finitely many experiments, after extracting their geometric incident-edge branch probabilities as above, the following construction gives the hypotheses of Lemma 10.3 simultaneously for all nonvanishing branches. Its readings take values in [0, M], and their limiting variables are the absolute values |Y | of the Brownian strand-boundary samples of the conditional mean profiles. No landing-side sign is conditioned upon.
